bib.title: Chapter 1. The Five Principles of Prompting (Prompt Engineering for Generative AI)

question: What small set of model-agnostic principles makes a prompt reliably yield useful results?
contributions: Five Principles of Prompting: Give Direction, Specify Format, Provide Examples, Evaluate Quality, Divide Labor
Worked product-name and Midjourney examples for each principle
A small A/B rating harness (thumbs up/down in Jupyter) for comparing prompt variants

results.claim: In the chapter's A/B test of a zero-shot prompt (A) against a few-shot prompt (B), five blind-rated responses each, the few-shot variant scored higher.
results.setup: Product-name prompt for shoes that fit any foot size; gpt-3.5-turbo with system message 'You are a helpful assistant.'; num_tests=5 per prompt; shuffled blind manual thumbs-up/down; prompt_B has two examples. Single run, one rater, no significance test.
results.note: Variant A score printed as 0.2. Format difference: A returned numbered lists, B comma-separated inline lists.

results.claim: Adding one example to a prompt can raise accuracy on some tasks from 10% to near 50% (citing the GPT-3 paper, Figure 1-8).
results.source: Brown et al., Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3)
results.setup: Read from the GPT-3 paper's in-context example figure; some tasks only; chapter gives no model size or task name.
results.quote: showing adding one example along with a prompt can improve accuracy in some tasks from 10% to near 50%!

limits: Examples use GPT-4 / ChatGPT Plus, gpt-3.5-turbo, Midjourney v6 and Stable Diffusion XL; the authors concede these may no longer be state of the art within months and that prompt templates rarely transfer between models.
The only quantitative test is 5 samples per variant, one rater, no significance test; the authors note manual rating is tedious and may not match the intended audience.
Claim that 'Hsieh et al., 2023' shows direction beats examples is cited with no number.
Context window and character limits quoted (6,000 chars Midjourney, 32,000 free ChatGPT, GPT-4 8,192 tokens, Claude 2 100,000, Gemini 1.5 1M) are dated.
The extracted PDF lacks Figure content, so figure data (1-8, 1-11, 1-13) are not in the text.
practices: Give Direction: describe the desired style in detail or reference a persona (role-playing, e.g. style of Steve Jobs); imagine what context a human would need (1. Give Direction).
Prewarm / internal retrieval: ask the model for best-practice advice first, then ask it to follow that advice in the same chat (1. Give Direction).
Insert trusted external best-practice rules into the prompt as context, accepting the longer-prompt cost (1. Give Direction).
Too much direction can conflict; when direction clashes with other elements, keep the more important one (1. Give Direction).

Specify Format: state the output format up front (JSON or YAML), leave the JSON structure uncompleted in few-shot examples so the model completes it, and parse with a JSON parser to trigger retries (2. Specify Format).
Reinforce format with a system message such as 'You are a helpful assistant that only responds in JSON' or the model's JSON/grammar parameter (2. Specify Format).
Provide Examples: zero-shot is weakest; one to three examples almost always help; past that, experiment with count and diversity; low diversity constrains the output (3. Provide Examples).
Try Give Direction before collecting examples, since good examples are harder to gather (3. Provide Examples).
Evaluate Quality: move from blind trial and error to blind, randomized thumbs-up/down ratings over multiple runs per prompt variant (4. Evaluate Quality).

Programmatic evaluation where ground truth exists: cost, latency, calls, classification, reasoning, hallucination, safety, refusals, adversarial, similarity (BLEU/ROUGE, vector distance) (4. Evaluate Quality).
Use rated outputs to update prompt examples or as fine-tuning data; compare responses side by side and use Elo for across-model comparison (4. Evaluate Quality).
Shorter prompts that perform equally cut cost and latency; many prompt elements prove superfluous (4. Evaluate Quality).
Divide Labor: split complex tasks into chained calls, e.g. generate names, then rate them in a second call; split ratings into clarity, memorability, USP (5. Divide Labor).
Append 'Let's think step by step' as in-prompt task division for reasoning gains and an audit trail (5. Divide Labor).
Meta prompting: use a model to write the prompt for an image model (5. Divide Labor).
Image prompts: use permutation prompting to evaluate combinations of format and details; fix the seed for reproducibility (4. Evaluate Quality).

terms.definition: the process of discovering prompts that reliably yield useful or desired results
the input you provide, typically text, when interfacing with an AI model
including rules or best practices in the prompt, e.g. asking the model first for advice then asking it to follow it
a prompt with no examples / one example / multiple examples
basic trial and error of running the prompt and seeing the results, with no feedback loop
a standardized set of questions with predefined answers or grading criteria used to test performance across models
input multiple directions or formats and generate an image for each combination
break problems into component parts and chain multiple AI calls together
using an AI model to generate a prompt for an AI model
providing a base image in the prompt, as an example for image generation (Stable Diffusion community term)
